title: Hooks engine
goal: A hooks engine that runs user- or project-configured commands at agent lifecycle points (before/after tools, prompt submit, stop, compaction) with strict timeouts, a clear blocking contract, and trust gating for project-supplied hooks.
scope_in: Config: user `<config dir>/hooks.json` and project `.centcom/hooks.json`: `{ hooks: { <Event>: [{ matcher?: string, command: string[], timeout_ms?: number }] } }`; events `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `Notification`.

Commands are argv arrays executed without a shell; JSON event on stdin (`{ event, agent_id, tool?: { name, input }, result?: ..., cwd }`); defaults: timeout 10 000 ms (max 60 000), stdout/stderr cap 64 KiB each, max 8 hooks per event, run sequentially in config order (user before project).

Exit-code contract: 0 = continue (stdout JSON optional); 2 = block (stderr text returned to the agent as the reason); any other non-zero = non-blocking error (logged, agent continues). Optional stdout JSON `{ decision: 'allow'|'deny'|'ask', reason?: string, updated_input?: object }` for `PreToolUse`; `deny` blocks, `allow` never overrides a permission-engine deny, `ask` forces approval.
`matcher` is a tool-name glob (`Bash`, `Edit|Write`, `mcp__github__*`) for tool events.
Trust gate: project hooks run only when `TrustStore.isTrusted('hooks', sha256(file bytes))`; changed file means untrusted again; `needsTrust` surfaced to the UI.
Child env: allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, TMPDIR) plus `CENTCOM_HOOK_EVENT`, `CENTCOM_AGENT_ID`; never tokens.
Integrates as a `PermissionGate` decorator for `PreToolUse` (runs before the permission engine and can only tighten) and as bus listeners for the other events.
scope_out: The permission engine itself: lane C015. Trust store implementation: lane C013.
A hook marketplace or remote hooks. Hooks that modify model output (not supported).
build_against: Tiny fixture scripts (node one-liners) written to a temp dir by the tests; fake clock for timeout tests; in-memory TrustStore.
interfaces: `createHooksEngine(deps: { fs: HooksFs; spawn: SpawnFn; trust: TrustStore; clock: Clock; bus: AgentBus; log: Logger; config: HooksConfig }): HooksEngine`

`interface HooksEngine { load(projectRoot?: string): Promise<{ needsTrust: PendingTrust[] }>; trust(file: string): Promise<void>; run(event: HookEvent, input: HookInput): Promise<HookOutcome>; gate(inner: PermissionGate): PermissionGate }`
`HookOutcome = { blocked: boolean; reason?: string; decision?: 'allow'|'deny'|'ask'; updatedInput?: unknown; errors: number }`.
acceptance: A `PreToolUse` hook exiting 2 with stderr `no force pushes` blocks the tool and the agent receives exactly that reason text; exit 1 is logged and does not block.
A hook printing `{decision:'allow'}` does NOT turn a permission-engine `deny` into allow (integration test with C015 stub): the combined outcome is deny.
A hook sleeping 20 s with `timeout_ms: 10000` is killed at 10 000 ms (fake clock; SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 2 s) and counted as a non-blocking error.
stdout of 1 MiB is truncated at 64 KiB and the hook is not failed solely for that; invalid JSON stdout from a hook that exited 0 is ignored with a warning.
Project hooks file is not executed (spawn count 0) until trusted; modifying one byte of the file untrusts it; user hooks run without prompting.
Matcher `Edit|Write` triggers for Edit and Write and not for Bash; `mcp__github__*` matches `mcp__github__create_issue`.
The spawned env contains `CENTCOM_HOOK_EVENT` and none of the poisoned variables from the parent (token/secret names).
9th hook for an event is ignored with a warning; execution order equals config order.
tests: matcher.test.ts, env.test.ts, argv-no-shell.test.ts (metacharacters in args are literal).
guardrails: MUST NOT run project hooks without local trust bound to the file hash; hooks are arbitrary code execution.
Hooks MUST NOT be able to loosen security: a hook `allow` cannot override a permission-engine or hard `deny`; `updated_input` is re-validated by the permission engine afterwards.
MUST spawn by argv without a shell; MUST NOT interpolate event data into command strings.
MUST NOT log hook commands, stdin payloads, stdout/stderr contents or tool inputs; log event name, duration, exit code.
Every hook is time-limited (default 10 s, max 60 s) and output-capped (64 KiB).
failure_modes: Hook binary missing -> non-blocking error `spawn_failed`, agent continues.
Hook crash/timeouts on `PreToolUse` -> do not block (fail open for hooks only because the permission engine remains the fail-closed control).
hooks.json invalid -> ignored with a warning; no hooks run.
notes: Event names follow the common agent-hook vocabulary; they are internal to the client and not a contract.
